items.question: After the blast aboard the New York City sludge ship Hunts Point, where was the missing senior engineer eventually located?
items.expected_answer: Before the fire department arrived at 1030, the chief engineer was found between the concrete dock and a wooden fender on the vessel's starboard side; he was declared dead at the scene.

evidence.quote: Before the arrival of the fire department at 1030, the chief engineer was found between the concrete dock and a wooden fender located on the starboard side of the vessel.
The chief engineer was declared dead at the scene by the responding New York City Fire Department paramedics.

items.notes: Tests retrieval of a narrative detail about the post-explosion search, phrased without the report's wording.

items.question: How long did firefighters take to put out the blaze that burned on deck after the explosion aboard the sludge vessel Hunts Point?
items.expected_answer: The premise is wrong: there was no fire after the Hunts Point explosion; instead, sludge burst out of the tank and covered the assistant engineer and the vessel's exterior.

evidence.quote: Following the explosion, there was no fire; however, sludge burst out of the tank and covered the assistant engineer and the exterior of the vessel.

items.notes: False premise of a post-explosion fire; note the casualty type in the summary table is listed as Fire/Explosion, which could mislead a system.
